full_judgment:
8. Mr. Fazlul Karim raised another point that when the trial of the case by the Sessions Judge was illegal and without jurisdiction, the appellate Court can only set aside or quash the judgment and order of the trial Court, but cannot send it back for retrial by a competent court. Mr. Karim in support of his view refers the case of Dharmasena vs King reported in Criminal Law Journal, 1950 Vol. 50 page 1997, the case of Abdul Ghani vs Emperor reported in the Indian Law Reports Vol. 29 page 412 and lastly, the case of Gopalkrishna Naidu vs State of Modhya Prodesh reported in AIR 1952 and Nagpur page 170. In the case reported in AIR 1952 and CrlLJ 1950, the view taken is that when the appellate Court finds that the trial of a case is without jurisdiction, the proper course is to quash or set aside the conviction. But in both the cases it is also held that such quashing of conviction shall not amount to acquittal. Of course, it is held in the AIR Nagpur case that the appellate Court under such circumstances cannot pass an order for re-trial. 

 9. We are of the view that the facts and circumstances of the above two reported cases are different from the facts and circumstances of the case before us. Moreover we have no intention to pass any order for retrial. In the facts and circumstances of the present case we are of the view that the trial Court had no jurisdiction to try the offence and the offences were triable by Special Tribunal constituted under the provisions of Special Powers Act, 1974. We find that there is no legal bar if the case is sent back for its trial by a court of competent jurisdiction. In the case reported in 51 CrlLJ 1950 as cited above, the appellate Court passed an order for a new trial after quashing the order of conviction. The Privy Council did not express any definite view to the effect that the action of the appellate Court was illegal or improper. In the case reported in ILR the court held the view that the trial was held by a Magistrate who had no jurisdiction to hold the trial and, as such, no trial has taken place and the Sessions Judge under such circumstances would not have passed an order for retrial.
